chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Alarm-clock pranks on the band bus
summary: Crawford recalls Jack Carruthers and Paul Webster hiding Big Ben alarm clocks in their bags on the bus.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Now, I wanted to talk at this point with you about --
-- personnel in the band, what you thought of them as players and as individuals, like Earl
Oh-oh. Got a good one for him.

Well, we used to travel by bus a lot. So Jack was always a mischievous guy. We'd be on the bus after a gig, going to another gig. And Jack for some reason found out about putting an alarm clock in his bag up in the rack. And we'd be sleeping in there, gone, and that doggone alarm clock would go off, the loudest Big Ben you ever heard in your life, wake everybody up. Pardon me just a minute.

Well, so -- well, that was fun, and Paul Webster thought he'd do one better. He stashed two Big Bens in his -- in his trunk, not his trunk but his bag. And those things went off rattling and waking everybody up, and that was his fun. Now, I got through with Paul, Jack and Paul. Jack was always up to something.

And Willie Smith was a little bit more -- he was full of fun also, but he was a little bit more on the society type. One of those Charleston, South Carolina, guys. Wilcox --
